name: Four-touch signal-triggered (DAG)
when_to_use: Signal coverage is dense enough that most contacts carry a recent, dated trigger - a relevant hire, a stack change, a public post. Selecting this without that coverage produces a sequence whose first touch waits on an event that never arrives.
rationale: A dated trigger buys relevance that no amount of copy can manufacture, and it decays. The whole cadence is compressed and the sequence abandons the contact outright if the signal goes stale, because a reference to a two-month-old event reads worse than no reference at all.
cites: research/01-discipline-and-pipeline.md (Frontier pattern 2026: sequence logic is event-driven, not calendar-driven)
research/04-psychology-nepq-persuasion.md §5.2 (3 follow-ups max; each adds a new angle; no guilt language)
research/01-discipline-and-pipeline.md (standard cadence: touch day 1, follow-up day 4, day 8, breakup day 11)
research/02a-operators-outbound.md (signal-triggered sequences 8-15% reply vs 2-5% static; time-to-first-touch under 2h for tier-1 signals)

send_window.why: A campaign rule. gtme-send materializes it per contact against their location.

nodes.intent: Open on the trigger itself, in the first line, then connect it to the problem it implies. Speed is the product here.
constraints: reference the trigger in the first sentence
never send if the signal is older than its freshness window
cites: research/02a-operators-outbound.md (signal-triggered sequences 8-15% reply vs 2-5% static; time-to-first-touch under 2h for tier-1 signals)

nodes.intent: Move from the trigger to the consequence: what this change usually creates downstream.
Answer the objection this persona raises, with proof drawn from a comparable situation.
Close the loop while the trigger is still recent enough to be worth mentioning once more.
constraints: state explicitly that this is the final message

nodes.intent: A person reads the reply and classifies it. The engine never does this.
nodes.why: A reply is not a yes. 'Who is this?' and 'send me pricing' are both reply_human and want opposite next moves. Automating this classification is the specific failure that killed most AI SDR deployments.
cites: research/02a-operators-outbound.md (50-70% of AI SDR contracts cancelled within 90 days - vendors automated volume without solving judgment)

nodes.intent: Answer what they actually asked, then hand over the product page as the single next step. This is the first touch in the whole sequence permitted to carry a product link.
constraints: reply in-thread, never a new thread
answer their question before sharing anything
exactly one link - the product page
no new pitch, no new pain
nodes.why: The cold stage earned attention by naming a problem. The warm stage converts it by removing work: one link, one next step.

nodes.intent: One short nudge if the share went unanswered. Offer a concrete time, then stop.
cites: research/04-psychology-nepq-persuasion.md §5.2 (3 follow-ups max; each adds a new angle; no guilt language)

nodes.note: Not-now is a real answer. Parked rather than pushed; re-entry is a human decision, not a timer.

engine_notes.durations: ISO-8601, measured from when the contact ENTERED the from-node, not from sequence start.
engine_notes.priority: Lower wins. Event edges must outrank the timeout edge on the same node.
engine_notes.no_model_call: Every message node is pre-rendered per contact by gtme-write. The engine selects and sends; it never generates.
